title: Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan deliver the goods in heist series 12 12 12 — read Empire's review

 12 12 12 Review
 People: Jamie Dornan Anthony Mackie Across 12 months of planning, 12 hours of execution, and 12 days after the crime, master thief Paul Galvin (Jamie Dornan) is tracked as he looks to pull off a billion-dollar bank robbery in Zurich. FBI Agent Jack Strickland (Anthony Mackie) is trying to stop him. by Amon Warmann | Published on 15th November 2026 at 4.55pm Follow Empire on Google Streaming on: Apple TV
 Episodes viewed: 8 of 8
 “A high-asset robbery, professionally conceived, is 12 months in planning, 12 hours in execution. A bank robber who’s not caught within 12 days… is not caught at all.” So begins almost every episode of 12 12 12 , a solid cops-and-robbers thriller created by Dudi Appleton and Jim Keeble. The grabby gimmick makes for a clever conceit in this series, which, at its best, is a fun addition to the small-screen heist-caper catalogue.
 Divided into the planning, the robbery and the takedown, each hour gives us a piece of each segment — with the odd time-skipping and rewinding liberty taken here and there — over the course of the eight-episode season. With this approach comes pros and cons: there is satisfaction in seeing how certain aspects of the heist come together, especially as new information and different vantage points force us to reframe what we’ve previously watched; but the structure not only means that the audience is frequently ahead of the characters — which dilutes the tension and investment at certain points — but that we also know the heist is successful from the get-go. It’s one thing to suspect that a crew of robbers are probably going to walk away with the goods, quite another when it’s explicitly confirmed before we see exactly how they managed it.
 Both actors put in convincing shifts here, shining brightest when bringing their characters’ conflicted interiorities to the fore.
 One aspect that does remain consistent throughout is the confident direction. TV veteran Kari Skogland ( The Falcon And The Winter Soldier , The Handmaid’s Tale ) is behind the camera for half of the episodes, while Takeshi Fukunaga ( Tokyo Vice , Shōgun ) and Ellen Kuras ( The Umbrella Academy ) split the other four. The on-location shooting adds a tactile quality to proceedings, giving the series a welcome visual panache.
 It also helps that the cop and robber don’t fit into neat good-guy and bad-guy boxes. FBI Agent Jack Strickland (Anthony Mackie) is powered by a vengeance that often has him stepping over the line, while the super-smart criminal Paul Galvin (Jamie Dornan) has his own righteous reasons for putting those he loves in danger. Both actors put in convincing shifts here, shining brightest when bringing their characters’ conflicted interiorities to the fore.
 The cast around them are a bit of a mixed bag: Agathe Rousselle is a striking and formidable screen presence for Dornan to face off with as Paul’s romantic partner Severine, but while Sallie Harmsen’s Swiss police officer Lena has a likeable-enough dynamic with Mackie’s G-man as she aids him in the investigation, she doesn’t have nearly enough to do. Most frustrating of all is Paul’s big brother Bobby (Jack Kesy), a hot-headed mess of a character who is consistently grating. That we get some explanation for his constant volatility never quite syncs with how reliably annoying he quickly becomes.
 Thankfully, that’s not true of the series as a whole, especially in the strong back half that introduces a character-altering twist. It’s not quite enough to elevate 12 12 12 ’s status to the other greats of the heist genre, but it does help make it worthy of a breezy binge-watch.
